record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: For which graph structures G(A) can one systematically determine a completely positive factorization A = B B^T of a completely positive matrix A, where B is entrywise nonnegative and G(A) is the graph with vertices 1,...,n and an edge between i and j exactly when i != j and a_ij != 0?

evidence.quote: Only partial results are known as to finding a factorization of A given that G(A) has a certain structure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A symmetric n×n real matrix A is called completely positive if there exists an entrywise nonnegative (not necessarily square) matrix B such that A = B B^T. The graph G(A) of a symmetric n×n matrix A is defined as the simple graph on vertex set {1,2,...,n} in which distinct vertices i and j are joined by an edge if and only if a_{ij} ≠ 0.

Problem: Characterize the graphs G with the following property, and for each such G provide a constructive procedure: whenever A is a completely positive matrix with G(A) = G, one can systematically (algorithmically) produce an explicit entrywise nonnegative matrix B such that A = B B^T. In other words, determine for which graph structures G a cp-factorization of every completely positive matrix A with G(A) = G can be obtained in a systematic way, and exhibit such a procedure.
artifact.status_search_result: Only partial results are known. Constructive cp-factorizations are available for special graph classes (e.g., triangle-free graphs, graphs whose blocks are cycles, certain chordal graphs), and general algorithmic approaches (Bomze's "Building a completely positive factorization", Riemannian smoothing methods, polynomial-optimization based methods) have been developed for arbitrary completely positive matrices, but a complete graph-structural characterization with a systematic factorization procedure remains open.

status_evidence.title: Building a completely positive factorization
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithmic approaches to constructing a cp-factorization without relying on graph structure.
status_evidence.claim: General-purpose cp-factorization methods exist but are not graph-structural characterizations.

status_evidence.title: On the cp-Rank and Minimal cp Factorizations of a Completely Positive Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Studies cp-rank and minimal cp-factorizations; partial results depending on structure.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural results on cp-factorizations are known.

status_evidence.title: Completely positive factorization by a Riemannian smoothing method
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical method for cp-factorization, not a graph-structural classification.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to address cp-factorization without resolving the graph-structural question.
